Verdict: the copy-first page-port direction is sound, with one real sequencing gap and one already-known, correctly-deferred one — not the four-alarm mismatch the ticket sprawl might suggest.

**The one thing that would actually bite: build [SFCC-743](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-743) before porting PLP/Home.** SFCC-80 (PLP grid) and SFCC-90 (Home) both explicitly *don't* own their own grid — SFCC-80's own description says "the product group grid component is covered in SFCC-743," and SFCC-743 is a separate, already-scoped `ProductCardGroup` organism (`display: 3/4/6`, `size`, `showTitleAndLink`, `showLink`, `title`, `linkLabel`) meant to be shared verbatim across PDP ("More from this category"/"Recommended for you"), PLP, and Home's featured-tiles row. SFCC-743 is currently Blocked and its own description leans on "ProductCard components (SFCC-236)" — which just shipped ([fb870d1](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/organisms/zimmProductCard/index.tsx)) — so it's plausibly next in line, though I'd confirm its actual blocker via the issue link rather than take my inference as fact. If PLP/Home get copy-first-ported and hand-roll their own "grid + header + view-more/shop-all" markup instead, that's duplicating a component the backlog has already named — exactly the DRY problem [conventions.md](.claude/rules/conventions.md) flags, and not premature abstraction since it's real, scoped, upcoming work, not a hypothetical. Sequence it: SFCC-743 organism first, then PLP/Home ports consume it.

**Two things I expected to be risks and checked in code — they're not:**
- **Quick-add-to-bag (SFCC-185 PLP, SFCC-497 Wishlist)** — already fully in the card's contract. `onAddToBag?: () => void` exists on both the `plp` and `wishlist` variation types and is wired straight through to [ZimmProductCardContent](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:117)'s bag button. Both tickets are page/basket-wiring work (call the real mutation, and for SFCC-497 specifically, remove-from-wishlist-on-success), not a card change.
- **Was/Now pricing (SFCC-464, SFCC-778)** — the card takes `currentPrice`/`originalPrice` as already-formatted strings; it has zero opinion on which backend mechanism produced them. That means SFCC-778's catalogue-price-rule path and the existing sale-pricebook path can both feed the card through the same kind of pure mapper the PDP already uses ([productInfo.ts](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/productInfo.ts), [variantScopedPrice.ts](overrides/app/pages/product-detail/variantScopedPrice.ts)) — reused/generalized, not reimplemented per page. One thing worth a quick visual check when that work starts: SFCC-464 specifies the "Now" price in **green**, and I haven't looked at `ZimmProductPrice`'s actual recipe in this session to confirm it matches that spec rather than a neutral/default treatment.

**One gap that's real but already correctly parked:** badges (SFCC-225/132). SFCC-225's own AC text says a badge "renders on the PDP/PLP" — not PDP-only — but [ZimmProductCardContent's docblock](overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/index.tsx:146) is explicit that it was built with **no badge slot**, calling it "a known, accepted gap, not something to fill by guessing a home for it." That's the right call given SFCC-132 is still Blocked with open questions as of today (badge count limit, Figma link unresolved). Nothing to do now — just don't let SFCC-80's PLP port improvise a badge treatment later; wait for SFCC-132 to actually resolve.

Net: the card-level architecture (SFCC-236) is holding up well against everything downstream. The only planning change I'd make is inserting SFCC-743 as an explicit step before the PLP/Home copy-first ports, rather than treating those page ports as the next thing in line.

content.text:
Think of the card we just built (ZimmProductCard) as a trading-card template — it's got slots for the photo, the name, the price, a little bag button, and it can be dressed up differently depending on where it's shown (homepage vs. category page vs. wishlist).

Now a bunch of other tickets want to *use* that template in different ways, and the question was: does the template hold up, or does something crack?

**One real thing to fix in the plan order:** PLP and Home don't just want single cards — they want a *row of cards with a title on top* (like "New Arrivals →" followed by 4 cards). That "row + title" wrapper is its own separate, not-yet-built ticket ([SFCC-743](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-743)). If we build the PLP page and the Home page *before* that wrapper exists, whoever builds each page will invent their own version of "row of cards with a title" — two slightly different homemade versions of the same thing, instead of one shared one. That's the kind of thing that quietly turns into double the maintenance later. **Fix: build that shared "row of cards" piece first, then have PLP and Home plug into it.**

**Two things that looked risky but turned out to be non-issues:**
- The "add to bag" button people want on PLP and Wishlist cards? Already built into the card. It's just not wired to actually add anything to the bag yet — that's plumbing work, not a redesign.
- The "sale price" ticket (show old price crossed out, new price in green)? The card just displays whatever price text it's handed — it doesn't care where that number came from. So that's someone else's job to calculate correctly, not a card change.

**One thing correctly left undone:** a "badge" sticker (like "Runway" or "Exclusive") on the card. We deliberately did *not* build a spot for it, and that's the right call — the design team hasn't even decided how many badges can fit on one card yet. Nothing to do here until that's settled.

So: no redesign needed on the card itself. Just make sure "build the shared row-of-cards component" happens before "build the actual PLP/Home pages," not after.

content.text:
Good question — it's neither of those exactly. Let me narrow it down.

It's **not** about the copy-first mechanical step (copying the base PLP/Home file into `overrides/`, converting to TypeScript, dropping in a `console.log` marker). That step is just relocating a file — no card logic gets written yet, so it doesn't touch this concern at all, regardless of what order anything happens in.

It's **not** about "build the entire PLP page" or "build the entire Home page" either. Most of those pages have nothing to do with the product card:
- Home has 6 sections total (hero banner, featured products, campaign links, shop-the-look, top categories, editorial/boutique duo) — only **1 of those 6** (the featured-products row) touches the card at all. The other 5 are totally unaffected by any of this.
- PLP is more central — the product grid basically *is* the page — so this concern covers more of it there.

**What it's actually about:** the one specific piece of code — wherever it gets written — that arranges *multiple* cards into a row with a title and "view more"/"shop all" link on top. Doesn't matter if that gets written as a small "just drop the card in where it's needed" task or as part of a big full-page build — if that specific "row of cards + header" logic gets hand-written directly inside the PLP page file and separately inside the Home page file, that's the duplication. Each page ends up with its own slightly-different homemade version of the same thing, instead of both using one shared piece.

So the practical dividing line is: placing a *single* card somewhere (e.g. proving it renders correctly with real data) doesn't hit this at all. The moment the work becomes "arrange several cards together with a heading," that's the part that should wait for (or be built as) SFCC-743, rather than being written fresh inside the PLP or Home page code.

- **Wishlist (SFCC-497)** — this one's actually not a group story at all, as far as I can tell. SFCC-743's own description lists its target pages as PDP, PLP, and Home — it doesn't mention Wishlist. So Wishlist wiring (the add-to-bag icon on each card) can likely proceed independently, regardless of what happens with SFCC-743.
- **PDP's "More from this category" / "Recommended for you"** — SFCC-743 name-checks these as intended consumers too, but I haven't found a specific ticket number for them yet in what I've pulled — worth tracking down before assuming they're covered.

So to directly answer: yes, you can proceed with copy-first porting the pages and wiring in individual card usage wherever a page just needs one card or a non-grouped layout. What's actually pending is narrower than "Home and PLP" — it's specifically **PLP's core grid** and **Home's featured-products section**, because those two are where the not-yet-built group wrapper (SFCC-743) is needed.

One more thing worth flagging while I'm in here, since you're the assignee: [SFCC-83](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/browse/SFCC-83) (Recently Viewed) describes itself the same way — "a shared component that renders a rail of product tiles, built once, reused across PLP/PDP/Cart." That's structurally the same shape as SFCC-743's ProductCardGroup, just possibly a rail instead of a grid. Might be worth checking with Jasmijn/Kiera whether Recently Viewed is meant to be a variant of SFCC-743 rather than a fourth separate "group of cards" component built from scratch.
